rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the highest-priority question is establishing a simple, well-understood baseline to anchor all subsequent comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible configuration: no image processing, no aggregation, no fusion, and a fast linear encoder (PCA). It provides a reference accuracy for the RNA modality with a standard representation. This baseline is essential for later experiments to quantify the marginal value of (a) adding an image modality, (b) switching to learned RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt), (c) moving to multiprofile with aggregation, and (d) different fusion strategies. Starting with the simplest model also minimizes confounding: any future improvement can be attributed to a specific added component rather than to an already-complex starting point. Under a 10-experiment budget, anchoring with the cheapest, most interpretable baseline maximizes the information gained per experiment and reduces uncertainty about the most fundamental design axis (which modality and representation carries the most signal).

The only completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) yields a low accuracy of ~48.5%, indicating the RNA-only baseline is weak. The highest-priority uncertainty is which modality carries the strongest discriminative signal. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest direct comparison to config_001: same profile setting (singleprofile), same 'no aggregation/fusion' simplicity, differing only in modality. If image accuracy substantially exceeds RNA, subsequent experiments should prioritize image encoders and multimodal fusion; if it is comparable or lower, we should invest in better RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) or multimodal combinations. Resolving this modality question early is critical because it determines the entire direction of the remaining 8 experiments and avoids wasting budget on a modality that is fundamentally weak.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 (config_010) is very weak at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. The key uncertainty is whether the linear PCA encoder is a bottleneck for the RNA signal. This experiment (config_004: rna_only, singleprofile, scvi_n200) isolates the effect of switching from a linear PCA encoder to a learned non-linear scvi representation while keeping profile setting identical to config_001. If scvi improves accuracy, it informs encoder choice for all downstream multimodal experiments; if not, PCA is sufficient and we can focus budget on profile/aggregation/fusion choices. This is the highest-information single-variable test available and the best use of experiment 3 with 7 remaining.

Evidence: scvi_n200 (0.5203) outperforms pca_n2000 (0.4849) in singleprofile RNA-only, and image-only is very weak (0.2079). The best current configuration is config_004 (scvi_n200, singleprofile). Uncertainty: whether multiprofile with aggregation can further improve over singleprofile for the best RNA encoder. This experiment (config_005) tests scvi_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation while holding the encoder fixed at the best-performing choice. It is the minimal logical extension of the current best result, and with 6 experiments remaining, establishing whether multiprofile helps before investing in transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion is the highest-value next step. If it improves, we can then test transformer aggregation (config_006); if not, we pivot to scgpt or multimodal exploration.

The current best (config_005, acc 0.650) uses rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool. The multiprofile+scvi_n200 combination showed a large gain over singleprofile (0.650 vs 0.520), confirming both are important. The key remaining uncertainty within this RNA-only direction is whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool for combining multiple profiles. Config_006 isolates exactly this: same encoder (scvi_n200), same multiprofile setting, only aggregation changes from avgpool to transformer. This is a clean single-variable comparison that will tell us which aggregation to carry forward into multimodal experiments. Under the 5-experiment budget remaining, resolving the aggregation choice now prevents wasting slots on suboptimal aggregation in later multimodal trials, making it the highest-information next step.

Evidence: Multiprofile RNA with scvi_n200 is the clear best setup so far (config_006: 0.653 acc), with multiprofile providing a large jump over single-profile (+0.13). Transformer aggregation marginally edges avgpool. Image-only is very weak (0.208). Uncertainty: scgpt, the only untested RNA encoder, has not been evaluated in any setting. This experiment tests whether scgpt can match or exceed scvi_n200 in the multiprofile + transformer setting that has proven most effective. Clarifying the best RNA encoder before moving to multimodal fusion is critical: if scgpt wins, subsequent multimodal experiments should use it; if scvi_n200 wins, we can confidently commit remaining budget to multimodal scvi_n200 configurations. This isolates the encoder variable while holding profile and aggregation at their best-known values, making it the highest-information experiment with 4 slots remaining.

The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 acc. The RNA modality is clearly dominant (0.48–0.65) while image-only is very weak (0.21 with resnet50). The key untested question is whether the image modality, despite its low standalone accuracy, provides complementary signal when fused with the strong RNA representation. config_032 is the most direct extension of the current best: it keeps scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer (the proven RNA pipeline) and adds resnet50 image features via concat fusion. This isolates the fusion benefit with the simplest fusion strategy. If it beats 0.653, the remaining 3 experiments can explore weighted fusion or ViT image encoder to push further. If it does not, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and can use remaining budget to fine-tune the RNA pipeline. This is the highest-value exploration step given 3 experiments remain.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 acc / 0.659 F1, a clear improvement over the best RNA-only multiprofile (config_006, 0.653). The only untested axis directly comparable to config_032 is the fusion method: config_033 is identical except it uses weighted fusion instead of concat. This is a clean single-variable A/B test that isolates whether learned/adaptive fusion weights can extract more signal from the image modality (whose standalone resnet50 accuracy was very low at 0.208, suggesting the image features may benefit from re-weighting). With 2 experiments remaining, resolving the fusion question first lets the final experiment target the image encoder (ViT-L vs ResNet50) with the confirmed best fusion strategy, maximizing the chance of finding the overall best configuration within budget.

The current best is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.713 accuracy. All other design axes have been well-explored: scvi_n200 > scgpt > pca, multiprofile >> singleprofile, transformer ≥ avgpool, and weighted > concat. The one major untested axis in the best configuration is the image encoder. ResNet50 alone was very weak (0.208), yet it still contributed ~6% over RNA-only when fused, suggesting a stronger visual encoder could yield further gains. config_039 replaces resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l while holding all other settings (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) constant, isolating the image-encoder effect. With only one experiment remaining after this, testing the highest-leverage single change to the best configuration is the most efficient use of the budget.

The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250). Evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder, multiprofile over single, transformer over avgpool, and weighted over concat (0.7131 vs 0.6878 with resnet50). The only untested single-variable ablation of the best configuration is config_038, which swaps weighted→concat fusion while keeping all other settings identical. While weighted fusion outperformed concat in the resnet50 setting, the interaction between concat fusion and the higher-dimensional ViT-L features is untested and could theoretically yield a different relative performance. As the final experiment, this clean one-variable comparison is the most informative use of the remaining budget: it either confirms weighted fusion's superiority across image encoders or reveals an interaction effect, and it is the closest untested candidate to potentially challenge the current best.
